Base change of triangles

Base change must carry the specified triangle of a functor over the base, not just its underlying functor. We spell out the calculation supporting base change of relative functors. Use the Chapter 1 structures and the conventions of Triangles over a base.

Fix \(p\colon S\to T\) and categories \(f\colon C\to T\) and \(g\colon D\to T\). Write \(r\colon C\times _T S\to C\), \(q\colon C\times _T S\to S\) and \(\tau \colon fr=pq\) for the chosen pullback data. If \(u=(h,\theta )\) is a functor from \(f\) to \(g\) over \(T\), form the cone with legs \(hr,q\) and matching \[ g(hr)\simeq (gh)r\xrightarrow {\theta r}fr\xrightarrow {\tau }pq. \] Its lift defines \(p^*u\). The second projection computation is its specified triangle over \(S\).

Supplementary Lemma 1. A comparison \(u\simeq _T v\) induces a comparison \(p^*u\simeq _S p^*v\).

Proof idea

Write \(v=(k,\psi )\) and let \(\alpha \colon h=k\) be the given comparison. Restrict \(\psi \cdot (g\alpha )=\theta \) along \(r\), and compare the two associations of the resulting composites. Pasting with \(\tau \) gives the matching equation for the two cones. This retains the right leg \(q\) and its identity comparison.

The formal construction performs this lift on the universal family of relative comparisons and evaluates at the given comparison. The resulting identification carries its compatibility over \(S\). This construction does not require identifying it with an independently chosen pointwise lift. □

Supplementary Lemma 2. Let \(a,b\colon X\to D\times _T S\) be equipped with triangles \(\beta _a\colon q_Da=t\) and \(\beta _b\colon q_Db=t\), where \(q_D\colon D\times _T S\to S\) is the second projection and \(t\colon X\to S\). Suppose \(\Phi \) compares their full induced pullback cones and its right component comes with a specified identification \[ \beta _b\cdot \Phi _{\mathrm {right}}=\beta _a. \] Then \(\Phi \) lifts to a comparison of \(a\) and \(b\) over \(S\). The cone comparison induced by this lift is identified with \(\Phi \), including its matching compatibility.

Proof idea

Use the identification-anima universal property of the pullback to lift \(\Phi \) with its prescribed image. Its right projection computation transports the displayed equation to the triangle equation of the lifted identification. The full image computation also compares the matching witnesses. Thus the same lift serves both the pullback calculation and the calculation over the base. □

Supplementary Lemma 3. There are comparisons over \(S\) \[ p^*(\operatorname {id})\simeq _S\operatorname {id}, \qquad (p^*v)(p^*u)\simeq _S p^*(vu) \] for composable functors \(u,v\) over \(T\). For composition, the resulting cone comparison recovers the comparison obtained by pasting the defining pullback computations.

Proof idea

For the identity, compare its defining cone with the original pullback cone. The unitor on the first leg and the identity on the second satisfy the matching equation by the triangle law.

For composition, restrict the defining cone of \(p^*v\) along \(p^*u\). Apply its computation comparison, then the one for \(p^*u\), and use the restriction and composition comparisons for the action on cones. This produces a full comparison with the defining cone of \(p^*(vu)\). Its right component satisfies the equation in Supplementary Lemma 2; checking that equation uses the actual second-projection computations defining the triangles. Reflection gives the desired comparison over \(S\), together with its full cone and triangle computations. □
